title: Mobile Phone Spectrophotometer Setup for Chlorophyll Experiment
author: Katharine E Hubbard
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bwfspbne

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Hardware
steps.instruction: Set up a well-lit workspace, preferably under natural light or with a lamp to minimize shadows and maximize contrast.

substeps.instruction: Fully charge the phone and unplug it from the charger to avoid electrocution risks when handling liquids.
Install a color picker app that provides numerical RGB values (e.g., 'ColorPicker' for iPhone or 'ColorGrab' for Android).

steps.title: Assemble Cuvette Holder
steps.instruction: Construct and secure the cuvette holder using the provided template and sellotape.

substeps.instruction: Sellotape the cuvette holder to the work surface.
Place and tape a piece of white card behind the cuvette holder.

steps.title: Configure Phone Position
steps.instruction: Position the phone so the color picker pointer is centered in the middle of the cuvette.

substeps.instruction: Rest the phone against a stable object (e.g., a mug or box) to ensure the position remains constant for all measurements.

steps.title: Test Solvent Compatibility
steps.instruction: Verify if the acetone-based nail polish remover (or 80% acetone) reacts with the plastic cuvettes.

substeps.instruction: Place 3 mL of nail polish remover into a cuvette and leave for 10 minutes.
If the plastic remains clear, use the remover directly.
If the plastic becomes cloudy or deforms, dilute the nail polish remover to 80% (e.g., 40 mL nail polish remover mixed with 10 mL water).

steps.title: Create Calibration Curve
steps.instruction: Establish a relationship between chlorophyll concentration and RGB values using a dilution series.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a dilution series of chlorophyll in cuvettes using nail polish remover (not water) as the solvent; label cuvettes clearly.
Place the 100% concentration cuvette in the holder with the transparent side facing the phone.
Record the RGB values using the color picker app.
Repeat for all dilutions in the series.
Plot a calibration curve with concentration on the x-axis and RGB value on the y-axis.

steps.title: Normalize RGB Data
steps.instruction: Convert raw RGB values to a positive relationship with concentration using one of two normalization methods.

substeps.instruction: Method 1 (General): normalized value = 1 - (RGB value / 255).
Method 2 (Relative to blank): normalized value = 1 - (sample RGB value / blank RGB value).
Plot a second calibration curve using these normalized values.

steps.title: Select Optimal Color Channel
steps.instruction: Determine which color channel (Red, Green, or Blue) shows the strongest relationship between concentration and RGB to use for subsequent experiments.

steps.title: Perform Leaf Chlorophyll Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract chlorophyll from plant material for measurement.

substeps.instruction: Put 3 mL of nail polish remover into a fresh cuvette.
Cut 3 cm² of leaf material into small pieces and place them in the cuvette, ensuring they are fully submerged.
Place the cuvette in the holder and record the RGB value for the chosen color channel.
Repeat for all replicates, maintaining consistent incubation times and leaf piece sizes (minimum 5 replicates per sample for t-tests).

steps.title: Prepare Chlorophyll Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Create a concentrated chlorophyll stock and a 10% dilution.

substeps.instruction: Pour 20 mL of nail polish remover into a plastic falcon tube labeled 'Chlorophyll stock'.
Cut approximately 8 medium-sized leaves (e.g., spinach) into small pieces (0.5 cm squares) and immerse them in the acetone; cap the tube.
Let the stock sit for ~30 minutes to allow chlorophyll to dissolve.
Pipette 2.5 mL of the extract into a new 50 mL tube and add 22.5 mL of acetone to reach a total volume of 25 mL; label as '10% chl stock'.
Let the 10% stock sit for 20 minutes to allow diffusion.
Transfer the acetone into a fresh cuvette, leaving the leaf material behind.
